# Pinned toolchain for both CI workflows.
#
# Lives in .github/ rather than the repo root because CI is its only consumer:
# nothing here is needed to work on the rules locally, and the workflows that
# install it sit in the same directory.
#
# Why this file exists: dev converts every Sigma rule to SPL with this exact
# toolchain, and the bytes it produces are what gets committed, atomic-tested,
# and eventually deployed -- so the conversion needs to be reproducible on its
# own terms, not tied to whatever happened to resolve on a given day. With
# floating versions that held because PyPI happened to serve the same release
# twice -- a property of the index, not of this repo.
#
# The prod *deploy* workflow (ci_prod_workflow.yml) does not install this file
# any more (register item 3.2, stage C): it used to re-run sigma_to_spl.py
# against the same Sigma source dev already converted, purely to prove the
# committed .spl hadn't drifted, which needed the identical converter pinned
# on both sides to mean anything. That reconversion is gone, replaced by
# verifying the build-provenance attestation dev already signed for the
# committed bytes, so prod has no converter to keep in step with dev's any
# more -- see .github/requirements-deploy.txt for what it installs instead.
# This file's pin is now dev's own reproducibility concern, not a two-sided
# agreement.
#
# pySigma is pinned even though nothing installs it directly: it is the engine
# that actually serializes the query text, so leaving it floating would defeat
# the pins on the two packages that wrap it.
#
# Deliberately NOT a full lock: transitive dependencies below these still
# float and there are no hashes. pip-compile / --require-hashes and automated
# version bumps belong to register item 2.11 (repo hygiene, dependabot).
#
# Resolved against Python 3.11 (the version both workflows set up).

pyyaml==6.0.3
jsonschema==4.26.0
sigma-cli==3.1.0
pySigma==1.5.0
pysigma-backend-splunk==2.1.0
requests==2.34.2
